screen: What changed because you reported it, the period fixes notice

markers.title: Addressed to the reporter, not to the auditor
markers.finding: 18 of the 41 respondents who answered the question, 44 per cent, said they never or rarely learn the outcome of a report, and restaurant visits confirmed that most team members never hear what corrective action followed (record fu-1).
markers.decision: The notice speaks to the person who reported, leads with what changed, and is posted where the team already stands.
markers.rejected: A safety scorecard or a percentage-closed figure, which answers the head office question rather than the reporter's.

markers.title: Every line names who reported it
markers.finding: A team member said minor incidents just get closed off, and only the more important ones are communicated back (record fu-2).
markers.decision: Each fix names the person who reported it, first name and initial, so the small reports appear beside the large ones and the credit is specific.
markers.rejected: An anonymous list of completed work, which is indistinguishable from maintenance the team never asked for.

markers.title: Days to fix is the number on the page
markers.finding: A team member had seen logged hazards changed quickly, and that was why he kept reporting (record fu-5).
markers.decision: Reported, fixed and days-to-fix are the only figures, with the median beneath them, so speed of response is what the notice reports.
markers.rejected: A count of reports received, which measures the team rather than the response to them.

markers.title: It says what is still late, and who to ask
markers.finding: Once a team member has told the manager, they have no visibility of what happens next or whether anything was logged (record aw-10).
markers.decision: The notice names the two actions still open and who to ask about them, so it works as a status the team can check rather than a selective good-news poster.
markers.rejected: Publishing only completed work, which would make the notice unreliable the first time somebody noticed an omission.

markers.title: Generated from the closed actions, typed once
markers.finding: Where reporting ran through the manager, the basics went onto paper and were entered at the end of the shift: double handling, and details got lost (record mf-8).
markers.decision: The notice is generated from the actions closed this period, using the words the manager already wrote at sign-off, so nothing is written twice.
markers.rejected: A manually written monthly poster, which is the first thing dropped in a busy period.
